text:
Anna (Support): FYI customer "AcmeAnalytics" reporting a large spike of 502/504s on hosted inference when using streaming responses. Started ~2026-02-18 11:10 UTC. They say the stream aborts mid-token, client sees ERR_HTTP2_STREAM_RESET. They've escalated and asked for repro + mitigation. Request IDs: req=acme-req-20260218-11:10:23 trace=trace-0a1b2c3d

Anna (Support): sample curl they ran (customer):
```
curl -v --http2 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-7b-v2","prompt":"<long prompt>"}' \
  https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate/stream
```
They get HTTP/2 200 for a few KB then a sudden reset, then 502/ERR on client.

infra-bot: Datadog alert: monitor.edge.gateway.502_rate crossed threshold (9% in 5m) for cluster=hosted-us-west2. Link: https://app.datadog/graph/edge-502s?from=... :warning:

Kevin_sre: Can you drop an envoy/error log line and the upstream host id? Need the exact envoy message (upstream reset vs upstream connection error). Also - any correlation with auth or billing timeouts?

Anna (Support): Pasted sanitized edge logs (excerpt):
```
[2026-02-18T11:10:24.123Z] envoy error: stream error code 0x2, message: "upstream reset before response complete" upstream_host: 10.12.34.56:443 response_code: 502 x-forwarded-for: 3.3.3.3
[2026-02-18T11:10:24.124Z] recv() failed: Connection reset by peer (104) while reading from upstream
[2026-02-18T11:10:24.124Z] request_id=acme-req-20260218-11:10:23 route="/v1/generate/stream" downstream_remote: client=52.11.22.33
```
They also included model host logs showing the model worker closed the connection after a long CPU stall: "worker: closing connection after write error: broken pipe"

Marc_runtime: Thanks. Two quick hypotheses: 1) very long streaming responses + h2 window exhaustion or kernel-level socket reset when model writes large chunks; 2) backend (model pod) is hitting per-connection buffer limits and the runtime decides to close. Does this only happen for streaming responses?

Anna (Support): Customer says it’s only for streaming (non-stream responses succeed). They attach a trace that shows initial data then abort at ~18s into stream. P95 latency for responses is fine for non-stream. 502 spike correlates with high token output sessions (very chatty).

Lisa_eng: Possible Envoy/NGINX interplay: if the model backend closes the socket while Envoy still thinks stream is open, Envoy interprets that as upstream reset and returns 502. Also we recently changed keepalive and http2 settings in the us-west2 edge pool. Could be timing.

Kevin_sre: We should capture a tcpdump from the edge to confirm who sent FIN/RST. Can someone run:
```
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/edge-acme.pcap host 10.12.34.56 and port 443 and host 52.11.22.33
```
And enable envoy debug for the connection id: `envoy.proxy.setLogLevel(trace)` temporarily on the affected node.

Anna (Support): I can get the customer to reproduce with a small script. They agreed to run a deterministic repro that keeps streaming until reset and provide the pcap + curl output.

Marc_runtime: In parallel I'll look at model-runtime logs and kernel dmesg on the worker host. Also check `ulimit -n`, `somaxconn`, and `net.core.rmem_max` / `wmem` settings on the executor. If the worker experiences write blocks due to backpressure it may close.

Anna (Support): Quick numbers: 502 rate went from 0.2% baseline up to 9% during the customer spike window (11:10-11:45). CPU on model pods spiked to 85-90% but not OOM. No crash loops. Memory steady.

Lisa_eng: Short-term mitigations for support:
- Turn off streaming for that customer's route (serve non-streaming chunked responses)
- Route high-output jobs to a fallback smaller model with same API shape
- Increase Envoy upstream idle/read timeouts for affected pool (eg set `upstream_read_timeout` higher)
- Throttle max tokens per request at the API ingress for streaming routes
These are config changes we can make quickly.

Kevin_sre: Agree. Also root cause data points we need: pcap showing who sent RST, envoy trace showing upstream reset reason, model pod logs (write errors), kernel logs (OOM or tcp_abort), and histogram of send_window/recv_window if possible.

Marc_runtime: I can push a canary change to the runtime to increase socket write buffer and enable backpressure-aware writes (small patch) — will test on a canary pool. ETA 2 hours if no blockers.

Anna (Support): Customer asked for a reproducible workaround now. I proposed disabling streaming for them and routing to fallback model. They'll accept immediate workaround while you do canary.

deploy-bot: Canaries scheduled: edge-us-west2 debug-log and keepalive bump -> canary start 2026-02-18T12:00 UTC, target nodes=2.

infra-bot: Added ticket INF-4521 and linked datadog graphs. Follow-ups: collect pcap, enable envoy trace, get model pod logs, update support playbook for streaming fallbacks.

Kevin_sre: Action items: (1) Anna to collect pcap + customer curl log (2) Marc to run runtime checks and push canary (3) Lisa to prepare Envoy timeout tweak and rollback plan. I'll stand by to flip debug logs and analyze pcaps.

Anna (Support): On it. I'll send the customer's pcap and curl output in this thread as soon as I have them. Thanks everyone, will update Acme with the streaming-off workaround now. :thumbsup:

Marc_runtime: I'll post the canary run results in ~2.5h with kernel/socket metrics.

Lisa_eng: Also adding note — check our recent change 2026-02-10 where we adjusted `http2_settings.max_concurrent_streams` on the edge; if lowered, streaming heavy clients could see unexpected resets. I'll validate config.

Anna (Support): ETA to customer for workaround: 15m. They'll confirm after we apply non-stream routing.

Kevin_sre: Thanks all. Please attach trace ids and request ids when you post logs so we can stitch them.

Anna (Support): Will do. Closing loop with Acme and will post repro artifacts here. :white_check_mark:
